subject: Purchase path advisory: invoice ownership, co-sell impacts for EduCloud (Marketplace vs Direct)
messages:
From: Maya Roy <maya@educloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: EduCloud Procurement <procurement@educloud.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick help: AWS Marketplace vs direct private offer (invoice / PO / support)

Hi Jonas,

We have a renewal coming up and procurement asked me to evaluate whether we should buy through AWS Marketplace (self-service or private offer) or engage Redwood directly with an enterprise contract. A few specific things they want clarified:

- Who issues the invoice and when (Marketplace invoice vs Redwood invoice)?
- Does a Marketplace private offer still allow us to use a PO and have a single SOW/invoice for internal accounting?
- Impact on co-sell credits/partner discounts if we route through marketplace vs direct?
- Support & SLA differences (is support bundled if purchased on marketplace?)
- Any implications for data residency / EU/US billing for our multi-region apps

We are EduCloud (education SaaS) — primarily US, some EU customers. Goal is predictable invoicing and minimal procurement friction. Would appreciate a one-page summary and your recommended path for a mid-sized seat + usage deal.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Roy
Head of Procurement
EduCloud

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Roy <maya@educloud.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick help: AWS Marketplace vs direct private offer (invoice / PO / support)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Putting a short operational comparison below and a recommended path at the end. Attached: one-pager that summarizes this for your procurement team.

High-level differences (operational):

1) Invoice & PO
- AWS Marketplace (public listing): AWS issues the invoice to you and collects payment. You get consolidated AWS billing; Redwood appears as the "seller" line item but AWS is the billing party. This is clean if your team requires centralized cloud spend on a single AWS invoice, but it complicates vendor-level accounting (no Redwood invoice).
- AWS Private Offer (via Marketplace private offers): still billed through AWS but a private offer can be made that mirrors negotiated pricing terms. You can usually provide a PO to AWS; procurement still records it as an AWS vendor invoice.
- Direct (Redwood invoice): Redwood issues invoice to EduCloud, we can accept your PO directly, and we can put specific billing language (SOW, invoice schedule) in the MSA. This is the simplest for vendor-specific accounting and for getting credits/discounts tied to Redwood directly.

2) Contracting cadence & flexibility
- Marketplace public: fastest for small purchases; limited negotiation; standard terms.
- Marketplace private offer: middle ground — pricing & term customization possible, but the contract is still anchored to marketplace flows and AWS billing processes.
- Direct: full negotiation on SOW, termination, liability caps, audit language, etc.

3) Co-sell and partner credits
- Listing on Marketplace does not prevent co-sell, but co-sell revenue share / credits are usually easiest to reconcile on direct deals where Redwood is seller-of-record. For marketplace purchases, partner crediting depends on marketplace partner programs and the paperwork for attribution.

4) Support & SLA
- If you buy via marketplace, support scope is defined by the listing. For enterprise-grade SLAs and a named technical account manager, direct contracts are typically more explicit (and we include higher-touch support options). Private offers can add some support commitments but still route billing through AWS.

5) Data residency & billing locality
- Marketplace billing is subject to AWS regional invoicing; if you need Redwood to be the invoice party for EU residency or local tax treatment, a direct Redwood invoice (or Redwood as seller-of-record in a private offer with local invoicing enabled) is preferable.

Recommendation for EduCloud (mid-sized, procurement-first):
- Short term (ease + speed): Use a private offer through AWS Marketplace to keep procurement happy with AWS billing and preserve negotiated pricing — minimal procurement friction.
- Medium/long term (vendor accounting + co-sell / support needs): Move to a direct Redwood invoice path (MSA + SOW) for renewals where you need vendor-level accounting, clearer co-sell attribution, or custom SLAs. We can coordinate a 6–12 month transition plan.

Next steps I suggest:
- I will share a one-page summary for procurement (attached).
- If you want a PO on the private offer, procurement should tell us the PO cadence and we will coordinate the private-offer flow with AWS Marketplace team.
- If you're leaning to direct, let's loop laura (contracts) to map the MSA/SOW timeline and kimberly for co-sell attribution requirements.

Attachments: educloud-marketplace-vs-direct-onepager.pdf (one-page comparison)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick help: AWS Marketplace vs direct private offer (invoice / PO / support)

Hi Maya — Laura from Contracts here. Quick answers:

1) Discounts & partner credits
- Private offer: You will still receive any negotiated Redwood discount in the private offer pricing, and co-sell attribution can be preserved if we submit the correct partner attribution (we'll need a simple attribution form). However, marketplace private-offer purchases typically flow through AWS programs for partner credits; some marketplace partner incentives require additional paperwork. We will coordinate with your procurement team to ensure the attribution is recorded in AWS.

2) Seller-of-record / Redwood invoice
- Seller-of-record on AWS requires specific marketplace onboarding and, in some cases, entity-level setup. It is sometimes possible for Redwood to be billed directly (Redwood as seller-of-record) for certain regions, but it depends on account setup and local tax rules. Practically:
  - Fastest path: private offer with AWS billing to you (AWS issues invoice). Procurement can treat the AWS invoice as the payment record.
  - If you need Redwood invoice for internal accounting, we can propose a direct Redwood invoice for the renewal term (move to direct MSA). Alternatively, we can evaluate whether a private-offer route with AWS enabling Redwood as seller-of-record in your region is feasible — that can take a few weeks to validate with AWS and finance.

Timeline for a private offer set-up
- Typical setup (private offer pricing + acceptance): 1–3 business days once terms are agreed and we raise the private-offer request with AWS.
- If you require Redwood as seller-of-record or special invoicing, timeline expands to 1–3 weeks while finance and AWS validate entity/tax details.

Attachments: redwood-private-offer-template.docx (template we use to trigger a private-offer flow)

If you want, Jonas will schedule a quick 30-minute call with procurement + our marketplace ops lead to kick this off and capture the PO details.

Cheers,
